There is always some variation I hear. "Buy seeds and gold to save yourself!" "Stock up on medicine and ammo!" I always find these "answers" to collapse as short sighted and ultimately ineffective as well as a waste of money. I mean really, we are talking about nothing short of the collapse of the industrial world and reverting to a world before when medicine was mass produced and available at every pharmacy with correct dosages and pure ingredients. We are talking about a world before bullets that have copper jackets and pins. We are talking about a world that required a scythe to mow the lawn, and your lawn had better be wheat or something, or you would be hungry.

Besides, what good is it to have seeds if you can't grow anything because you never learned? What good is having a cabinet full of emergency medicines that go out of date in a year or two and you don't even know how to use them? What if "collapse" becomes bad enough that you need" those medicines just five years after they expired and were thrown away? Isn't that a waste of valuable resources that would have been better spent on something else?

I mean even buying water filters is ineffective eventually. How do you replace them?

So we shouldn't be looking to "buy" anything to save us. We should be learning how to MAKE what we need to save us. We should all know how to produce the absolute basics in life. I don't mean specialty medicines, your cherry quinoa you just can't live without, or those triple stitched angus bullhide hiking boots either. Unless you have a medical condition or you have a specific one in the family, don't worry about it.

If you have something that runs in the family, (asthma, high blood pressure, diabetes) look for things that will prevent and treat them. There are herbs, dietary choices, and even breathing techniques that help those. You can not buy yourself more time...you can only delay the inevitable. Instead face the inevitable and learn to handle it.

Learn how to make your staple foods. That means your breads, milk, eggs, butter, vegetables and fruits. Just enough to stay alive.

Learn how to clean water without a special filter you picked up from the store.

Learn how to cut and split wood as well as care for the tools to do that.

Learn how to be a mid-wife, doula, and herbalist for the general aches and pains everyone gets.

Learn how to fix your house with trees and hand tools.

Once you have done all that and have the tools to do all that, sure buy some gold and specialty seeds. After all, you have this survival crap by the balls then.

Finally, there are less fish in the streams, less deer in the woods, and a whole lot less squirrels than when I was a kid. In fact, the only "meat" I see in abundance is snake. So if you intend to hunt your food, when everyone else is hungry too, expect to go hungry too. Just my two cents.

By the way...all of my children are learning these skills. Someone once called them "princes and princesses" of poverty. We'll see who is the prince and princess when everyone else is starving and they have fields of food for their family' s dinner table. To the poor starving man or woman, they would be as kings and queens.
Does anyone really think buying seeds and gold will save them?

If you can't survive without your emergency kit then there's not much hope for you. That doesn't mean you shouldn't have one or two or that you shouldn't have a secure long term storage location that's trapped and powered.

I've found that knowing how to perform maintenance on tools is where most people fall down, I've gone hiking with people and they have damaged their gear before the first weekend because they were being heavy handed and didn't look after the kit. Knowing how to sharpen edges for different tasks, knowing how to fix cracks in wooden tools or get dents out of metal ones before either leads to a piece of scrap instead of a hatchet.

If you're finding less wildlife than you remember then just head further out, cities have expanded and that means the wilderness is further away. I went into the hills near me and they were near quiet compared to how they were growing up, but I drove up to the mountains near my brother's house and it was much more busy. Rabbits all over and even the odd badger within eyesight from his back garden. That said if people are expecting meat to be a staple food then they are going to be disappointed, even the most ardent fishers are going to find shortfalls unless they maintain reliable farm plots year on year.

Put it this way, if a company as money grubbing and unethical as Microsoft starts handing out free stuff, the only reason they are doing that is because it benefits them in some way.

Microsoft has always charged a premium for their OS, so you have to ask yourself: why are they stopping now? Why this 1 year free upgrade period?

It's clearly because they want as many people using Windows 10 as possible, and people are more likely to upgrade if they think something is free, than if they know they have to pay for it. Same reason MS has made D12 Win 10 only: to force Gamers to upgrade if they want to play the latest eye-popping titles built around D12.

If a company is that eager for you to be using their latest product, you know something more is going on behind the scenes.

Microsoft's push to get everyone on Windows 10 isn't, in any way, related to the TPP. The timing is simply coincidental. that's not to say that; if there are provisions in the TPP that benefit Microsoft, they won't push an update that takes advantage of that.

There are a number of reasons that MS would want everyone to be running a single version of it's OS that have nothing to do with the TPP. some good, some bad.

Only having to support a single OS makes MS job of bug fixing, issue tracking, and support much easier. Right now MS has to continue to support several different versions of Windows (7, 8, 10, 2008, 2012, and legacy systems like XP that are still in use). Each OS has it's own support system which costs a lot of money and time to maintain. This is a huge drain.

MS will be collecting data from it's users and selling that information to create a new revenue stream for themselves. Companies like Google generate a huge amount of revenue by gathering, analyzing, and selling user data. MS has the ability to look over you shoulder at everything you do, consolidate that data, and sell it off to the highest bidder.

MS has decided that they will no longer be bringing out new versions of the Windows OS. They will be moving to a continuous upgrade system. There are two things that you can take from this.

  1. They believe that they have taken the NT core platform as far as it can go and there is no longer a reason to further develop the system.
  2. They are moving to a subscription based model for windows where users will pay a monthly fee to use the OS.

Personally, I think that Microsoft has realized that the market for the Windows desktop OS is starting to drastically shrink. Most people are moving towards phones and tablets (A section of the market that MS is not doing that well in) which cover most of their computing/online needs. Even more importantly (For Microsoft), most business applications are moving to web based online services (If they haven't moved over already). This means that there isn't as much of a need for a massive OS to support business applications on the desktop. When an application is shifted online, any OS with a modern browser can use it.

I'm guessing that MS is in the process of transitioning its efforts towards it's cloud based services. During this transition they will focus on consolidating the desktop OS division, maximizing revenue through subscription services, and getting users use to having their OS spy on them.

On r/BWF, everyone has conflicting goals that they fail to notice.

The overwhelming majority want to get jacked without lifting weights, yet they attempt to accomplish it by working up to advanced pole dancing and party tricks.

The two do not logically relate.

Let's go back to the beginning: you want to get muscular without lifting weights.

Okay. What is required to get muscular?

  1. Adequate tension

  2. Time under tension

  3. Recovery (protein, sleep)

Sweet.

Let's look at some basic moves for your upper body.

  • Handstand push ups
  • Pull ups
  • Dips
  • Rows, especially feet elevated

These ALL have you handling most or all of your weight in different planes of motion. In other words, tension is adequate.

Now you need time under tension and recovery, which means doing 999 sets of 999 reps, eating 50 pounds of lean protein and sleeping for 14 hours. No seriously though, each move you train you should shoot for like 50-100 reps total per workout, absolutely no fewer than 20. If you did less than 20 reps overall, you didn't even exercise.

What about your core?

Leg raises, V-ups, planks, dragon flags. Do lots of them. Eat protein. Sleep.

What about your legs?

Do deep step ups until you fall down and can't get up again. Eat protein. Sleep.

What about your posterior chain?

It's notoriously hard to train with BWF, but separate moves exist for traps (inverted shrugs), lower back (superman), glutes and hamstrings (glute bridge, glute ham raise). Alternately, you could just get a barbell or kettlebell and use that. Train with absolutely idiotic volume. Eat protein. Sleep.

How should I program my moves?

It doesn't really matter. Schedule yourself so you train everything 1-2x a week, beyond that it's all personal preference.

Should I increase resistance by training one arm decline pinky tip bodyweight lat raises with one foot elevated, along with other Cirque du Soleil moves?

NO, that's stupid. Your weight is constant, therefore anything you do to increase resistance means putting your full weight on fewer muscles. Taken to its logical conclusion, you'd be doing a routine of 100% isolation moves where you work every single muscle with some kind of bizarre lever. That kind of thing makes for good party tricks but it is not wise to do that to your joints, and the more advanced you get at that sort of training, the more complex it will be. Instead of working chest, triceps and shoulders with a simple move like a dip, you'll now have to do separate but more difficult moves for each of these. You'll do 60 weird lever moves trying to get 5% more strength while developing full body tendonitis. It's simpler and more ergonomic to increase intensity by doing more reps per set, doing more total sets, resting less between sets and playing with your rep tempo.

In closing what I'm saying is, if you're doing BWF because you want to get more muscular, you should probably do the opposite of common programs like StartBodyweight. Just do fairly simple things for dozens and dozens of reps and actually eat like a bodybuilder. You do not need to train planches to get big shoulders. You do not need to train levers to have a strong core. As usual, 99% of what the internet is telling you is totally wrong and unnecessary.
